validated_results.title: Intake of individual fatty acids and risk of prostate cancer in the European prospective investigation into cancer and nutrition.
validated_results.reason: Prospective EPIC cohort of cancer-free men estimating dietary intake of individual fatty acids, including butyric acid, with incident prostate cancer risk.

extraction.comparison_type: per 1 SD higher intake of butyric acid (4:0), risk of advanced stage prostate cancer
extraction.population: Men free from cancer at recruitment in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition

sample_size.excerpt: 142,239 men from the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition who were free from cancer at recruitment were included.

cases.excerpt: After an average follow-up of 13.9 years, 7,036 prostate cancer cases and 936 prostate cancer deaths were ascertained.

effect_size.excerpt: There was evidence of heterogeneity in the association of some short chain saturated fatty acids with prostate cancer risk by tumor stage (p<sub>heterogeneity</sub> < 0.015), with a positive association with risk of advanced stage disease for butyric acid (4:0; HR<sub>1SD</sub> = 1.08; 95%CI = 1.01-1.15; p-trend = 0.026).

confidence_interval.excerpt: There was evidence of heterogeneity in the association of some short chain saturated fatty acids with prostate cancer risk by tumor stage (p<sub>heterogeneity</sub> < 0.015), with a positive association with risk of advanced stage disease for butyric acid (4:0; HR<sub>1SD</sub> = 1.08; 95%CI = 1.01-1.15; p-trend = 0.026).

validated_results.reason: Prospective ARIC cohort of cancer-free men assessing dietary betaine intake and incident total and lethal prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: tertile 3 vs tertile 1 of betaine intake, lethal prostate cancer
extraction.population: Men without a cancer diagnosis at baseline in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study

sample_size.excerpt: We included 6,528 men (24.4% African American) without a cancer diagnosis at baseline (1987-1989) followed through 2012.

cases.excerpt: Choline intake was not associated with total (n = 811) or lethal (n = 95) PCa risk overall or by race.

effect_size.excerpt: Choline intake was not associated with total (n = 811) or lethal (n = 95) PCa risk overall or by race. Betaine intake was inversely associated with lethal (tertile 3 vs 1, HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.35-1.00, p trend = 0.04), but not total PCa risk; patterns for lethal PCa were similar by race.
